draft.title: Testing for gases
card: A glowing splint (a wooden stick with a glowing tip but no flame) bursts back into flame in oxygen.
When carbon dioxide is bubbled through limewater, the clear liquid turns milky.
A lit splint held at the mouth of a test tube of hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop.
Each test gives a result that only one of these three gases gives, so the result tells you which gas is in the tube.
draft.remember: Match the gas to its test: glowing splint relights, limewater turns milky, squeaky pop.

a.q: Zoe bubbles a gas through limewater and the liquid turns milky. Which gas is it?
a.why: Limewater turning milky is the test for carbon dioxide. Oxygen is tested with a glowing splint, so it does not cause this change.
a.clue: Which gas is linked to limewater?

b.q: Sam holds a glowing splint in a test tube of gas. It bursts into flame. He then holds a lit splint at the mouth of a second tube and hears a squeaky pop. Which gases are in the first and second tubes?
b.why: A glowing splint relighting shows oxygen. A squeaky pop from a lit splint shows hydrogen. The tubes are not the other way round, because the squeaky pop is the hydrogen test, not the oxygen test.
b.clue: Match each splint result to its gas.
